title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 295
text:
51. Since the offence was introduced in December 2015, the volume of offences reported to the
police has increased from 4,246 for year ending March 2017 to 41,626 for year ending
March 2022232 (98% of those prosecuted that year being male233).

52. The Family Court at High Court level, endorsed by the Court of Appeal in Re H-N and Others
(Children)(domestic abuse: findings of fact hearings), 234 has observed that coercive control
requires an evaluation of a pattern of behaviour in which the significance of isolated incidents
can only truly be understood in the context of a much wider picture. The Court of Appeal
considered that the primary question in many cases where domestic abuse is alleged is
likely to be “whether the evidence establishes an abusive pattern of coercive and/or
controlling behaviour... irrespective of whether there are other more specific factual
allegations to be determined.” This question is important because of the impact that such a
finding may have on the assessment of any risk involved in continuing contact.
